title: Chapter 131: I Know What I'm Doing
html:
The figures created through the Dollmaker’s Talent were profoundly unsettling. With twenty-four of them standing or sitting throughout the sealed classroom, even Chen Ge had no desire to linger.

I can’t open Mu Yang High School carelessly. If these twenty-four lingering spirits lose control, they might literally frighten someone to death. Because he had crafted each mannequin himself, Chen Ge could feel how profoundly the school uniforms had changed them. They seemed to have acquired souls; the figures before him no longer felt like props, but people.

Budget and staffing constraints kept most Haunted Houses from placing more than ten actors in one scenario. Chen Ge had worried about the same problem, but it was now solved: this modest set alone contained twenty-four professional performers. That was a truly high-end attraction.

Even I’m excited. This Two-Star Scenario might make the Haunted House famous throughout Jiujiang!

After finishing the arrangement of the sealed classroom, Chen Ge placed the student nametags that littered the lectern inside the paper box.

Mu Yang High School has only one entrance and no separate exit, so the old escape challenge won’t work. I need a new rule.An idea came to him: he could hide the twenty-four name tags throughout the scenario. Visitors must find every tag within twenty minutes. Winners receive a full refund and a cash prize. That should encourage people to enter while adding both interactivity and fun.

As the Haunted House expanded, Chen Ge had been searching for ways to make it more engaging. The name-tag hunt seemed worth a trial run.

I need to add more elements like this. My ultimate goal isn’t merely a frightening Haunted House, but an entire horror-themed park.

While hiding the name tags, Chen Ge discovered that Mu Yang High School had expanded. A new junction branched off at the corridor’s end, leading to three adjoining, weathered rooms numbered 302, 303, and 304.

The One-Star Trial Mission A Room of Three had added these apartments beside Mu Yang High School. The scenarios blended seamlessly, though the corridors had become noticeably narrower.

Every scenario will expand until the entire underground garage is full. Their paths will overlap and form a true Maze of Terror.

Chen Ge returned to the first floor, brushed the dust from his clothes, and opened the front gate. Warm sunlight touched his skin. It was perfect weather for a day at the park.

Xu Wan arrived around 9:00 a.m. Chen Ge sent her to apply her makeup and prepare Minghun. As attendance grew, the Haunted House became New Century Park’s only attraction with a line. To keep things moving, Chen Ge asked Uncle Xu to assign an available employee to the ticket booth. To his surprise, Uncle Xu came himself.

“We don’t have many spare employees, and I’m free. Should I work inside the ticket booth?”

“No need. Sell them however you’re comfortable.”

Leaving ticket sales to Uncle Xu, Chen Ge returned to the staff break room. He painted Mu Yang High School’s introduction and rules onto a wooden board using fake blood. When he carried it outside, excitement rippled through the line.

“A new scary scenario to experience!”

“This introduction sure is creepy.”

“A school horror story! This, I like!”

The new sign immediately captured the crowd. Since admission cost the same, everyone near the front requested the new scenario.

“Everyone, please listen.” Chen Ge propped the board beside the entrance. “This new scenario is extremely frightening. It contains professional actors and some of the finest equipment and props in the country. During its trial run, two employees from a rival horror studio accepted the challenge and secretly filmed the set, hoping to plagiarize it. Instead, they recorded something terrifying. Both are still in the hospital!”

Standing nearby, Uncle Xu was speechless. He could not understand why Chen Ge recited such a grim history with pride, as though nearly frightening visitors to death were an achievement.

“Tell us what they caught on camera!”

“You think we are that gullible to believe people might get sent to the hospital from a visit to the Haunted House?”

“Boss, don’t waste your breath! We are playing this scenario!”

“If I do not enter this scenario today, I am not a man!”

Once the crowd settled, Chen Ge continued. “I mention this because the new scenario is not open to everyone. Only visitors who have completed an earlier scenario may enter.”

To challenge Mu Yang High School, visitors first had to complete either Minghun or Murder by Midnight. Chen Ge had always intended to divide scenarios by their fear rating.

“That’s daylight robbery!” Protests erupted the moment he announced the rule. “Every scenario requires another ticket. If that isn’t forced spending, what is?”

“Has the success gotten to your head?!”

“I came because of the good online review, but what you are doing is incredibly immoral!”

“This Haunted House has too many rules. I’ll just leave! Happy now?”

Chen Ge had expected the backlash. Once everyone had vented, he slapped the wooden board. “I’m not trying to cheat you. The twenty-yuan ticket proves that. To demonstrate my sincerity, let’s make a wager.”

He placed his unused prize money beside the sign. “Here is twenty thousand yuan in cash. I hid twenty-four student name tags inside Mu Yang High School. Find all of them within twenty minutes, and the money is yours!”

“A twenty-yuan ticket for a twenty-thousand-yuan prize? That’s a thousandfold return!”

“How do we know how many nametags you have actually hidden inside the scenario? What if you have only hidden twenty-three nametags? Doesn’t that mean no one will win the reward?”

It was a fair question, but Chen Ge could not be bothered to argue. “If any of you walk out normally, I’ll answer that.”

The twenty-four tags were concealed in obscure corners, several where no ordinary visitor would ever think to look.

“Such conceit!”

“Why is that even though I know this is a cheap trick, I still have the urge to give it a try?”

“Let me!”

Excitement reached a boiling point. Chen Ge entrusted the prize money to Uncle Xu.

“Today is the first official day for both the scenario and its rules. Since we haven’t advertised it yet, Mu Yang High School will be open to everyone today—no prerequisite scenario required. You’ve heard the prize. One challenger at a time, one attempt per person, and the name tags will move each day. Who wants to claim twenty thousand yuan?”

The previously boisterous crowd fell silent. People glanced at one another, but no one stepped forward. At the back of the line, a group of six huddled in discussion. After a while, five approached him.

“Boss, we don’t want to attempt the challenge. We only want to experience the scenario. Can all five of us enter together?” their leader asked. The scheme was obvious: five would scout the scenario, then the sixth would use their information to attempt the name-tag hunt.

Chen Ge recognized their attempt to cheat but did not mind. “Of course. All five may enter together. One reminder: please don’t take photographs or videos. You might frighten our friends from the other side.”

“Five tickets—here’s one hundred yuan.” The young man smiled, paying no attention to the warning.

Chen Ge accepted the money and gave the five visitors his most “professional” smile. “Thank you. Please follow me.”

The visitors found his smile reassuring. Uncle Xu, however, shivered and hurried over to intervene.

He whispered, “These are ordinary visitors. They’ve done nothing to us, so be careful. Make sure everyone comes out safe.”

“Uncle Xu, do not worry. I know what I am doing.”

Chen Ge gently moved him aside, but the promise only made Uncle Xu more anxious. “Who are you fooling? You said the same thing last time, and those two poor kids are still in the hospital. Fei Youliang screams every midnight, asking who his wife will be. Everyone in the hospital knows him now!”
